title: Post-deploy circuit-breaker & model warmup validation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and automated verifier to run immediately after private (VPC) deployment or runtime upgrade. The verifier must: 1) confirm API readiness endpoints return wheel-of-health for route shards, 2) exercise model load and inference paths to populate KV cache and warm up optimized kernels, and 3) validate circuit-breaker and graceful-degradation behavior under limited capacity. The goal is to reduce post-deploy incidents caused by cold caches, kernel thrashing, or cascading request queues in customer VPCs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A GitHub Actions workflow (infra/qa) can be triggered via Terraform output to run the verifier against the new VPC endpoint. 2) The verifier returns PASS if: API readiness endpoints OK, 5 representative models load to >90% memory health and pass simple generation smoke prompts within latency SLOs, KV cache shows hits after warmup steps, and circuit-breaker trips and recovers as configured. 3) Alerts/rollback hooks defined for failures and integrated with the deployment pipeline.
runbook_steps: 1) After terraform apply, collect outputs: vip_endpoint, verifier_api_key, service_namespace. (tf output -json)
2) Create a short-lived canary traffic policy using the deployment API to send 5% traffic to the canary pool.
4) Execute staged warmup: n=50 synthetic prompts for each model -> wait for KV cache stabilization -> re-run sample latency tests.
5) Trigger simulated overload: run stress script at 1.5x nominal qps to validate circuit-breaker trips and redirects to fallback variant.
6) On PASS upload run artifact and results to the deployment ticket, tag runtime release. On FAIL follow rollback criteria and open incident channel.
terraform_notes: Add a boolean output postdeploy_verifier_trigger_url and store verifier_api_key in AWS SecretsManager with expiration. New module: redwood_vpc_postdeploy_verifier which wires outputs from vpc_service and dedicated_load_balancer. Ensure IAM role for verifier has ephemeral read access to KMS-wrapped keys for test signing.
model_load_plan: Warmup uses a prioritized corpus derived from recent request logs (edge-sampled to preserve PII protections). Plan: stage 1: low concurrency imports to seed KV cache; stage 2: medium concurrency to allow kernel JIT and scheduler stabilization; stage 3: verification generation set to exact tokens to validate output shape is correct. Use small sequence lengths first (32 tokens) then ramp to observed p95 sequence lengths.
smoke_test_scenarios: Authentication handshake: API key rotate and validate token acceptance
Simple generation: 5 prompts per model with deterministic seeds to validate model weights loaded
Embedding check: identical input returns stable embedding shape and magnitude range
Rate-limited path: ensure 429s are produced under quota and circuit-breaker triggers at configured queue depth
KV cache hit validation: repeated prefix calls show hit-rate increase >60% after warmup
monitoring_checks: Grafana panel: per-model memory usage and resident set stability (link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/vpc-health)
SLOs: 95th latency < 220ms for small/base models during smoke test window
Alert: model_load_errors > 0 for 5 minutes => fail run
Alert: sustained queue length > 3x baseline for 2 minutes => trigger rollback
Audit: store verifier logs to s3://redwood-postdeploy-logs/${service_namespace}/${timestamp} for 30 days
progress: 2026-02-10: Ticket created. Initial scope and acceptance criteria drafted.
2026-02-11: Discussed approach with infra and runtime teams. Decided on 3-stage warmup and a circuit-breaker threshold of 75% queue depth.
2026-02-13: POC verifier script implemented (tools/postdeploy_verifier v0.1). Added terraform module scaffold redwood_vpc_postdeploy_verifier in infra repo.
2026-02-15: Security requested a key-handling review. Marcus to provide PR with SecretsManager integration.

2026-02-17: Ran smoke run against staging vpc-qa environment (infra PR #4123). Observed KV cache hit rate improvement from 12% to 68% after warmup. Noted 1 model that failed kernel init on p3dn-24; added mitigation to limit concurrency for that model.
2026-02-18: Updated runbook and terraform notes based on staging run. Marked security_review_required=true and requested formal review.
risks: Warmup traffic may leak sensitive prefixes if sampling isn't properly redacted - ensure sampling pipeline strips PII.
Aggressive warmup can cause noisy neighbor effects in multi-tenant shared infra - cap concurrency for early stages.
False negatives if verifier uses only synthetic prompts - include a small set of sanitized real-traffic samples.
Key provisioning: improper SecretsManager permissions could leave verifier unable to authenticate causing false FAILs
